summary: Agenda lists today's events in time order, with a line that marks where now falls in the day. When a person opens an event, the notes the agent prepared for it slide in underneath, along with an optional action such as joining the call. It suits an assistant that gets people ready for their meetings.
use: When an assistant prepares briefing notes before each meeting
When a home screen should show what is left of today at a glance
When a person needs a join or open button next to the context for a call
When past events should stay visible but step back from the ones still to come
features: Each row shows the time, title, a quiet detail line and avatars for the people attending.
Items marked `past` fade back, and the now line with the `now` time sits right after the last past item.
Opening an item reveals its `notes` one by one; items without notes do not open.
An `action` adds a pill at the end of the notes, like "Join in 48 min", that calls its own `onClick` without closing the row.
Only one item is open at a time, and you can control which with `open` and `onOpenChange` or let each row toggle itself.
The corner tag counts the events for you unless you pass your own `count` text.
a11y: Each event is a native button, so it is reachable with Tab and opens with Enter or Space.
Events that have notes carry `aria-expanded`, which reports whether their notes are open.
Attendee avatars are marked `aria-hidden`, so screen readers skip the initials.

faq.q: How do I have the agent open its notes for the next meeting on its own?
faq.a: Control the component with `open` and `onOpenChange`, then set `open` to that item's key when the agent is ready. The example on this page does exactly that a moment after it loads.

faq.q: Where does the now line go?
faq.a: It goes after the last item marked `past`, labelled with the `now` string you pass. Leave `now` out and no line is drawn.

faq.q: Can the notes contain links or formatted text?
faq.a: Yes. `notes` is an array of React nodes, so each note can be plain text or your own markup. Each note gets a small spark icon in front.
